title: Chronograph: admin-action timeline + escrowed attestation workflow
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Build a production-grade timeline service (Chronograph) that records administrator actions, access events, and configuration changes with cryptographic attestations and automated escrow snapshots per-residency region. The service should provide tamper-evident evidence bundles for audits, automated retention enforcement aligned with customer residency policies, and a reporting endpoint for compliance teams.

Scope:
- Record admin events (create/delete/privilege-change), config edits (route/model/policy), and access-granting operations.
- Per-customer residency tag and per-region storage targets.
- Periodic, incremental escrow snapshots: compact evidence bundle + signature, pushed to region-specific object stores with read-only lifecycle rules.
- Cryptographic commitments: Merkle root over the day's timeline plus an HSM-signed timestamp attestation.
- Retention enforcement: orchestrate lifecycle policies (short-lived vs. long-lived) and automated expiration actions with audit trail.
- Reporting: generate machine-readable evidence manifests for auditors and an admin-facing dashboard summary.
- Playbook for forensics: tools to reconstruct sequences, export canonized bundles, and verify signatures locally.

Out of scope for this ticket: full enterprise legal escrow process and third-party archival escrow transfers (follow-up). Not implementing cross-account replication logic beyond region residency mirroring in this phase.

Technical notes & trade-offs:
- Chose Merkle over append-only sequence numbers to enable efficient partial proofs for slices of history; trade-off is added complexity during ingest to compute incremental roots.
- Snapshot cadence: hourly for high-volume customers, daily for low-volume — balances cost and evidentiary granularity.
- Storage durability: use region-local object stores with object-lock style retention flags where available; for clouds that lack object-lock, fallback to signed, time-bound manifests and separate notarization.
- KMS/HSM integration: sign attestation payloads with customer-key-aware HSM keys where available; else use Redwood notarization key and record key provenance in the manifest.

Implementation tasks (high level):
1) Schema: define canonical event envelope (timestamp, actor, action, target, before/after, residency_tag, request_id, token-level metadata).
2) Ingest pipeline: append-only write into Chronograph service with low-latency ack; secondary worker computes rolling Merkle tree shards.
3) Snapshot & escrow job: bundle daily/hourly shards, generate attestations, push to region-specific escrow bucket + set immutability/retention flags if supported.
4) Evidence manifest API: retrieval endpoint that returns signed manifest and pointers to objects.
5) Orchestration: retention rule engine (policy store + enforcement tasks).
6) Verification tooling: CLI to fetch bundle, verify signatures, and reconstruct event timeline.
7) Dashboard integration: surface retention state, last-escrow timestamp, and any failed attestations in Console.

Deliverables: design doc, prototype ingest + snapshot job, escrow push for at least two cloud regions, evidence manifest API, verification CLI, Console tiles for status.

See design reference: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Chronograph+Design (draft).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical event envelope documented and approved by PM and Security
Ingest service accepts events with residency tags and persists append-only records
Hourly/daily snapshot job produces signed evidence bundles and uploads to region-specific buckets
Uploaded bundles include a signed manifest (Merkle root + attestation) and are immutable or marked for enforced retention where possible
Evidence manifest API returns verifiable pointers and signatures; verification CLI can validate a bundle end-to-end
Console shows per-customer last-escrow timestamp, retention policy, and any escrow failures
Unit and integration tests for ingestion, snapshotting, signing, and manifest retrieval
